content_of_post_to_answer: Why do people feel so much pressure when sitting in reserved seats, even when they're technically allowed to?
answer: The pressure comes from confusing “allowed” with “socially unquestionable.” A reserved seat gives you a legitimate claim, but other passengers may not know why you have it, so you can feel as though you must justify yourself before anyone even asks. The awkwardness is often less about the seat than about being visibly entitled to something others might think you don’t deserve.
